title: Giving up Cass Tech to stay with the band
summary: With the show rehearsals it was too hard to keep both, so he left school in the eleventh grade despite his principal's letter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Just about this period, I had passed the aptitude test at Cass Tech, the technical high school in Detroit. And it was difficult for me to keep the job and go to school, because I had to rehearse the show two days every other week

-- we had to rehearse the production. So I had to make a decision. I said, 'Well, now, I'm going to be a musician, that's for sure, so I just want to stay on this job' -- because it was the best job in Detroit at the time, you know. So I gave up school in Eleventh Grade. I gave it up. I haven't really regretted it. In fact, my high school principal, Mister Sanders, back in Jackson at Lanier High School, he wrote me a letter and told me to just come back and go through the graduation exercises, you know, he said 'because you're going to need a diploma.' And I said, 'Thank you very much, but I'll just leave it like it is.'
